🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Elke Sommer, the German-born actress and Golden Globe winner who became one of the defining screen stars of the 1960s, has died at 85.

Sommer died of heart failure on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at her home in Bel Air, Los Angeles, her stepson Sebastian Walther told the German outlet Bild. She would have turned 86 on November 5.

Born in Berlin on November 5, 1940, Sommer was discovered after winning the Miss Viareggio beauty contest in Italy at age 17 and was spotted by director Vittorio De Sica. She went on to a film career that spanned nearly six decades.

Her Hollywood breakthrough came opposite Paul Newman in The Prize (1963), a performance that won her the Golden Globe for Most Promising Newcomer. She is perhaps best remembered as Maria Gambrelli opposite Peter Sellers in A Shot in the Dark (1964), the second film in the Pink Panther series.

Her other films included The Victors (1963), Boy, Did I Get a Wrong Number! (1965) with Bob Hope, Deadlier Than the Male (1967), The Wrecking Crew (1969), and Mario Bava's Lisa and the Devil (1972). She later became known as a painter and remained a fixture of European television and public life. Her final credited acting role came in 2017.

Sommer's death comes three months after the death of her husband of 32 years, Wolf Walther, who died earlier this year after a battle with cancer.

Sources: Page Six (via stepson Sebastian Walther to Bild); Die Welt; Sweden Herald.
